summary:
Every wildfire season demands rapid decisions. VestApp transforms satellite data into actionable intelligence. We integrate thermal anomalies from MODIS and VIIRS with real-time meteorological variables, equipping teams with clear metrics and reliable data exports.

VestApp: Precise space monitoring to protect our environment.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO OR HOW DOES IT WORK?

- Harmonizes NASA Satellites: Fuses MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) into unified 1 km² grid cells, eliminating 56.6% of duplicate hotspots across a 26-year timeline (2000–2026).

- Dual-Horizon Prediction: Combines immediate fire physics (30-30-30 rule and +1h/+3h tactical wind propagation cones) with 72-week (~17 months) seasonal ignition forecasting based on climate cycles (ENSO).

- Automated Multi-Role Alerts: Evaluates live weather and satellite data to dispatch tailored early warnings via email with distinct physical criteria for firefighters, farmers, and neighbors.

WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

- Eliminates False Alarms: Removes overcounting so emergency teams deploy water and personnel to real fire perimeters instead of duplicate satellite points.

- 17-Month Foresight: Predicts exact seasonal danger windows months ahead, giving agencies time to mandate firebreaks and organize budgets before fires start.

- Instant Clarity: A 1-click toggle translates complex radiometric jargon into plain citizen language so anyone can act immediately.

WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

- Life Safety in Interface Zones: Provides rural and suburban communities a critical 1-to-3 hour evacuation head start before flames reach residential areas.

- Aligned with the UN Sendai Framework: Advances global disaster risk understanding (through 26 years of continuous data) and proactive early warning.

- Democratized Satellite Data: Delivers enterprise-grade NASA earth observation intelligence directly to volunteer brigades and citizens for free.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE USED

- NASA Assets: NASA FIRMS Near Real-Time API, MODIS (Terra/Aqua), VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20/21), and SRTM 30m elevation models.

- Meteorological Data: Open-Meteo & Meteomatics APIs (real-time wind vectors, relative humidity, temperature).

- Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic, NumPy, Pandas, SQLite local cache, and a secure SMTP email dispatch engine.

- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet with CartoDB Dark Matter tiles, and Recharts.

HOW IS IT CREATIVE?

- Dynamic Plain-Language Switch: Allows instant real-time toggling between scientific NASA terminology and empathetic civic phrasing across all maps, tables, and KPIs.

- Unified Micro-Tactical & Macro-Seasonal AI: Connects ground-level physical wind cones for active fires with long-range 72-week climate trend predictions on a single interface.

- Double-Encoded Universal Accessibility: Uses the Okabe-Ito colorblind palette paired with distinct geometric shapes (triangles, diamonds, circles, squares) so heat severity is never communicated by color alone.

WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

- Sensor Resolution Gaps: Mathematically normalized the point spread functions between MODIS and VIIRS to produce an unbroken, comparable 26-year historical record.

- Alert Fatigue Prevention: Filtered notifications through strict physical criteria per user role to ensure people only receive alerts when genuinely at risk.

- Universal Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AAA): Integrated 7:1 high contrast, font scaling, full keyboard navigation, and reduced motion modes.

- Ethical Governance: Maintained human-in-the-loop design; the platform provides decision support while explicitly leaving combat and evacuation commands to official authorities.
